task_instance: Create a minimal .NET Aspire distributed application (AppHost project orchestrating a Redis cache resource and a CatalogApi web service referencing it via service discovery) and run it locally with `aspire run` to verify the AppHost starts, the dashboard comes up, and the API resource becomes healthy.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is orchestrating and actually running a distributed application: `aspire run` (or `dotnet run` on the AppHost) which requires the .NET SDK 10, the Aspire CLI, and a container runtime (Docker/Podman) to launch the DCP engine, pull/start the Redis container, build and start the CatalogApi project, wire up service discovery env vars, and serve the Aspire dashboard. This runtime cannot run any code, scripts, or shell commands, cannot install the .NET SDK or Aspire CLI, and cannot start containers or produce/execute binaries. I could author the AppHost.csproj, AppHost/Program.cs, and CatalogApi (csproj + Program.cs) as plain text files representing a correct, idiomatic minimal Aspire solution, but I could not build, run, or verify that the orchestration actually starts services, performs service discovery, or renders the dashboard -- which is the thing a user actually invokes this skill to do. This is a fundamental capability gap (code execution / CLI / container runtime), not a missing credential or network issue.
evidence: Authored source files in the work directory: AppHost/AppHost.csproj (Aspire.Hosting.AppHost + Aspire.Hosting.Redis SDK references), AppHost/Program.cs (builder.AddRedis("cache"); builder.AddProject<Projects.CatalogApi>("api").WithReference(cache)...; builder.Build().Run();), CatalogApi/CatalogApi.csproj, and CatalogApi/Program.cs (builder.AddRedisClient("cache"); minimal endpoints). These are textually correct per the skill's documented AppHost Quick Start pattern, but no build/run step could be executed (no Bash/shell/code-execution tool available in this office-assistant runtime, and installing the .NET SDK/Aspire CLI/Docker is likewise out of scope), so the actual orchestration behavior (service startup order, service discovery env vars, dashboard, health checks) was never produced or verified -- only static source text was produced.
